Return True if bool(x) is True for all values x in the iterable.

If the iterable is empty, return True.

async anext(aiterator[, default])

Return the next item from the async iterator.  If default is given and the async
iterator is exhausted, it is returned instead of raising StopAsyncIteration.

globals.label: any
globals.documentation:
Return True if bool(x) is True for any x in the iterable.

If the iterable is empty, return False.

globals.documentation:
Return an ASCII-only representation of an object.

As repr(), return a string containing a printable representation of an

globals.label: bin

'0b1010101010101010101010'

globals.documentation:
bool(x) -> bool

Returns True when the argument x is true, False otherwise.
The builtins True and False are the only two instances of the class bool.
The class bool is a subclass of the class int, and cannot be subclassed.

globals.label: breakpoint
globals.documentation:
breakpoint(*args, **kws)

Call sys.breakpointhook(*args, **kws).  sys.breakpointhook() must accept
whatever arguments are passed.

bytearray(int) -> bytes array of size given by the parameter initialized with null bytes

bytes(iterable_of_ints) -> bytes
bytes(string, encoding[, errors]) -> bytes
bytes(bytes_or_buffer) -> immutable copy of bytes_or_buffer
bytes(int) -> bytes object of size given by the parameter initialized with null bytes
bytes() -> empty bytes object

globals.label: callable
globals.documentation:
Return whether the object is callable (i.e., some kind of function).

Note that classes are callable, as are instances of classes with a
__call__() method.

globals.label: chr
globals.documentation: Return a Unicode string of one character with ordinal i; 0 <= i <= 0x10ffff.

Convert a function to be a class method.

A class method receives the class as implicit first argument,

globals.documentation:
Create a complex number from a string or numbers.

If a string is given, parse it as a complex number.
If a single number is given, convert it to a complex number.
If the 'real' or 'imag' arguments are given, create a complex number

contributors and the copyright notice.

interactive prompt objects for printing the license text, a list of

delattr(x, 'y') is equivalent to ``del x.y``

globals.documentation:
dict() -> new empty dictionary
dict(mapping) -> new dictionary initialized from a mapping object's
    (key, value) pairs
dict(iterable) -> new dictionary initialized as if via:
    d = {}

globals.label: dir
globals.documentation:
dir([object]) -> list of strings

If called without an argument, return the names in the current scope.
Else, return an alphabetized list of names comprising (some of) the attributes
of the given object, and of attributes reachable from it.

globals.label: divmod
globals.documentation: Return the tuple (x//y, x%y).  Invariant: div*y + mod == x.

globals.label: enumerate
globals.documentation:
Return an enumerate object.

  iterable
    an object supporting iteration

globals.label: eval
globals.documentation:
Evaluate the given source in the context of globals and locals.

The source may be a string representing a Python expression
or a code object as returned by compile().
The globals must be a dictionary and locals can be any mapping,

globals.label: exec
globals.documentation:
Execute the given source in the context of globals and locals.

The source may be a string representing one or more Python statements
or a code object as returned by compile().
The globals must be a dictionary and locals can be any mapping,

globals.label: filter
globals.documentation:
filter(function or None, iterable) --> filter object

Return an iterator yielding those items of iterable for which function(item)
is true. If function is None, return the items that are true.

globals.label: float
globals.documentation: Convert a string or number to a floating-point number, if possible.

globals.label: format
globals.documentation:
Return type(value).__format__(value, format_spec)

Many built-in types implement format_spec according to the
Format Specification Mini-language. See help('FORMATTING').

globals.label: frozenset
globals.documentation:
frozenset() -> empty frozenset object
frozenset(iterable) -> frozenset object

Build an immutable unordered collection of unique elements.

globals.label: getattr
globals.documentation:
getattr(object, name[, default]) -> value

Get a named attribute from an object; getattr(x, 'y') is equivalent to x.y.
When a default argument is given, it is returned when the attribute doesn't
exist; without it, an exception is raised in that case.

globals.label: globals
globals.documentation:
Return the dictionary containing the current scope's global variables.

NOTE: Updates to this dictionary *will* affect name lookups in the current
global scope and vice-versa.

globals.label: hasattr
globals.documentation:
Return whether the object has an attribute with the given name.

This is done by calling getattr(obj, name) and catching AttributeError.

globals.label: hash
globals.documentation:
Return the hash value for the given object.

Two objects that compare equal must also have the same hash value, but the
reverse is not necessarily true.

globals.label: help
globals.documentation:
Define the builtin 'help'.

This is a wrapper around pydoc.help that provides a helpful message
when 'help' is typed at the Python interactive prompt.

globals.label: hex
globals.documentation:
Return the hexadecimal representation of an integer.

>>> hex(12648430)
'0xc0ffee'

globals.label: id
globals.documentation:
Return the identity of an object.

This is guaranteed to be unique among simultaneously existing objects.
(CPython uses the object's memory address.)

globals.label: input
globals.documentation:
Read a string from standard input.  The trailing newline is stripped.

The prompt string, if given, is printed to standard output without a
trailing newline before reading input.

globals.label: int
globals.documentation:
int([x]) -> integer
int(x, base=10) -> integer

Convert a number or string to an integer, or return 0 if no arguments
are given.  If x is a number, return x.__int__().  For floating-point

globals.label: isinstance
globals.documentation:
Return whether an object is an instance of a class or of a subclass thereof.

A tuple, as in ``isinstance(x, (A, B, ...))``, may be given as the target to
check against. This is equivalent to ``isinstance(x, A) or isinstance(x, B)
or ...`` etc.

globals.label: issubclass
globals.documentation:
Return whether 'cls' is derived from another class or is the same class.

A tuple, as in ``issubclass(x, (A, B, ...))``, may be given as the target to
check against. This is equivalent to ``issubclass(x, A) or issubclass(x, B)
or ...``.

globals.label: iter
globals.documentation:
iter(iterable) -> iterator
iter(callable, sentinel) -> iterator

Get an iterator from an object.  In the first form, the argument must
supply its own iterator, or be a sequence.

globals.label: len
globals.documentation: Return the number of items in a container.

globals.label: license
globals.documentation:
interactive prompt objects for printing the license text, a list of
contributors and the copyright notice.

globals.label: list
globals.documentation:
Built-in mutable sequence.

If no argument is given, the constructor creates a new empty list.
The argument must be an iterable if specified.

globals.label: locals
globals.documentation:
Return a dictionary containing the current scope's local variables.

NOTE: Whether or not updates to this dictionary will affect name lookups in
the local scope and vice-versa is *implementation dependent* and not
covered by any backwards compatibility guarantees.

globals.label: map

Make an iterator that computes the function using arguments from
each of the iterables.  Stops when the shortest iterable is exhausted.

With a single iterable argument, return its smallest item. The

next(iterator[, default])

Return the next item from the iterator. If default is given and the iterator
is exhausted, it is returned instead of raising StopIteration.

globals.label: object
globals.documentation:
The base class of the class hierarchy.

When called, it accepts no arguments and returns a new featureless
instance that has no instance attributes and cannot be given any.

globals.label: oct
globals.documentation:
Return the octal representation of an integer.

>>> oct(342391)
'0o1234567'

globals.documentation:

file is either a text or byte string giving the name (and the path
if the file isn't in the current working directory) of the file to
be opened or an integer file descriptor of the file to be

globals.label: ord
globals.documentation: Return the Unicode code point for a one-character string.

globals.label: pow
globals.documentation:
Equivalent to base**exp with 2 arguments or base**exp % mod with 3 arguments

Some types, such as ints, are able to use a more efficient algorithm when
invoked using the three argument form.

globals.label: print
globals.documentation:
Prints the values to a stream, or to sys.stdout by default.

sep

end

Property attribute.

    function to be used for getting an attribute value
  fset

globals.label: range

range(start, stop[, step]) -> range object

Return an object that produces a sequence of integers from start (inclusive)
to stop (exclusive) by step.  range(i, j) produces i, i+1, i+2, ..., j-1.

globals.label: repr
globals.documentation:
Return the canonical string representation of the object.

For many object types, including most builtins, eval(repr(obj)) == obj.

globals.label: reversed
globals.documentation: Return a reverse iterator over the values of the given sequence.

globals.label: round
globals.documentation:
Round a number to a given precision in decimal digits.

The return value is an integer if ndigits is omitted or None.  Otherwise
the return value has the same type as the number.  ndigits may be negative.

globals.label: set
globals.documentation:
set() -> new empty set object
set(iterable) -> new set object

Build an unordered collection of unique elements.

globals.label: setattr
globals.documentation:
Sets the named attribute on the given object to the specified value.

setattr(x, 'y', v) is equivalent to ``x.y = v``

globals.label: slice
globals.documentation:
slice(stop)
slice(start, stop[, step])

Create a slice object.  This is used for extended slicing (e.g. a[0:10:2]).

globals.label: sorted
globals.documentation:
Return a new list containing all items from the iterable in ascending order.

A custom key function can be supplied to customize the sort order, and the
reverse flag can be set to request the result in descending order.

globals.label: staticmethod
globals.documentation:
staticmethod(function) -> method

Convert a function to be a static method.

A static method does not receive an implicit first argument.

globals.label: str
globals.documentation:
str(object='') -> str
str(bytes_or_buffer[, encoding[, errors]]) -> str

Create a new string object from the given object. If encoding or
errors is specified, then the object must expose a data buffer

globals.label: sum
globals.documentation:
Return the sum of a 'start' value (default: 0) plus an iterable of numbers

When the iterable is empty, return the start value.
This function is intended specifically for use with numeric values and may
reject non-numeric types.

super() -> same as super(__class__, <first argument>)

globals.label: tuple
globals.documentation:
Built-in immutable sequence.

If no argument is given, the constructor returns an empty tuple.

globals.documentation:
type(object) -> the object's type
type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

globals.documentation:
vars([object]) -> dictionary

Without arguments, equivalent to locals().
With an argument, equivalent to object.__dict__.

globals.documentation:
zip(*iterables, strict=False) --> Yield tuples until an input is exhausted.

   [('a', 0, 0), ('b', 1, 1), ('c', 2, 2)]

globals.label: Counter
globals.documentation:
Dict subclass for counting hashable items.  Sometimes called a bag
or multiset.  Elements are stored as dictionary keys and their counts
are stored as dictionary values.

>>> c = Counter('abcdeabcdabcaba')  # count elements from a string

globals.label: defaultdict
globals.documentation:
defaultdict(default_factory=None, /, [...]) --> dict with default factory

The default factory is called without arguments to produce
a new value when a key is not present, in __getitem__ only.
A defaultdict compares equal to a dict with the same items.

globals.label: deque
globals.documentation:
deque([iterable[, maxlen]]) --> deque object

A list-like sequence optimized for data accesses near its endpoints.

globals.label: bisect_left
globals.documentation:
Return the index where to insert item x in list a, assuming a is sorted.

The return value i is such that all e in a[:i] have e < x, and all e in
a[i:] have e >= x.  So if x already appears in the list, a.insert(i, x) will
insert just before the leftmost x already there.

globals.label: bisect_right
globals.documentation:
Return the index where to insert item x in list a, assuming a is sorted.

The return value i is such that all e in a[:i] have e <= x, and all e in
a[i:] have e > x.  So if x already appears in the list, a.insert(i, x) will
insert just after the rightmost x already there.

globals.documentation:
Insert item x in list a, and keep it sorted assuming a is sorted.

If x is already in a, insert it to the right of the rightmost x.

Optional args lo (default 0) and hi (default len(a)) bound the

globals.label: insort_left
globals.documentation:
Insert item x in list a, and keep it sorted assuming a is sorted.

If x is already in a, insert it to the left of the leftmost x.

Optional args lo (default 0) and hi (default len(a)) bound the

If x is already in a, insert it to the right of the rightmost x.

Optional args lo (default 0) and hi (default len(a)) bound the

methods.label: capitalize
methods.documentation:
Return a capitalized version of the string.

More specifically, make the first character have upper case and the rest lower
case.

methods.label: casefold
methods.documentation: Return a version of the string suitable for caseless comparisons.

methods.label: center
methods.documentation:
Return a centered string of length width.

Padding is done using the specified fill character (default is a space).

methods.label: count
methods.documentation:
S.count(sub[, start[, end]]) -> int

Return the number of non-overlapping occurrences of substring sub in
string S[start:end].  Optional arguments start and end are
interpreted as in slice notation.

methods.label: encode
methods.documentation:
Encode the string using the codec registered for encoding.

encoding
  The encoding in which to encode the string.
errors

methods.label: endswith
methods.documentation:
S.endswith(suffix[, start[, end]]) -> bool

Return True if S ends with the specified suffix, False otherwise.
With optional start, test S beginning at that position.
With optional end, stop comparing S at that position.

methods.label: expandtabs
methods.documentation:
Return a copy where all tab characters are expanded using spaces.

If tabsize is not given, a tab size of 8 characters is assumed.

methods.label: find
methods.documentation:
S.find(sub[, start[, end]]) -> int

Return the lowest index in S where substring sub is found,
such that sub is contained within S[start:end].  Optional
arguments start and end are interpreted as in slice notation.

methods.label: format
methods.documentation:
S.format(*args, **kwargs) -> str

Return a formatted version of S, using substitutions from args and kwargs.
The substitutions are identified by braces ('{' and '}').

methods.label: format_map
methods.documentation:
S.format_map(mapping) -> str

Return a formatted version of S, using substitutions from mapping.
The substitutions are identified by braces ('{' and '}').

methods.label: index
methods.documentation:
S.index(sub[, start[, end]]) -> int

Return the lowest index in S where substring sub is found,
such that sub is contained within S[start:end].  Optional
arguments start and end are interpreted as in slice notation.

methods.label: isalnum
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is an alpha-numeric string, False otherwise.

A string is alpha-numeric if all characters in the string are alpha-numeric and
there is at least one character in the string.

methods.label: isalpha
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is an alphabetic string, False otherwise.

A string is alphabetic if all characters in the string are alphabetic and there
is at least one character in the string.

methods.label: isascii
methods.documentation:
Return True if all characters in the string are ASCII, False otherwise.

ASCII characters have code points in the range U+0000-U+007F.
Empty string is ASCII too.

methods.label: isdecimal
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is a decimal string, False otherwise.

A string is a decimal string if all characters in the string are decimal and
there is at least one character in the string.

methods.label: isdigit
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is a digit string, False otherwise.

A string is a digit string if all characters in the string are digits and there
is at least one character in the string.

methods.label: isidentifier
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is a valid Python identifier, False otherwise.

Call keyword.iskeyword(s) to test whether string s is a reserved identifier,
such as "def" or "class".

methods.label: islower
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is a lowercase string, False otherwise.

A string is lowercase if all cased characters in the string are lowercase and
there is at least one cased character in the string.

methods.label: isnumeric
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is a numeric string, False otherwise.

A string is numeric if all characters in the string are numeric and there is at
least one character in the string.

methods.label: isprintable
methods.documentation:
Return True if all characters in the string are printable, False otherwise.

A character is printable if repr() may use it in its output.

methods.label: isspace
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is a whitespace string, False otherwise.

A string is whitespace if all characters in the string are whitespace and there
is at least one character in the string.

methods.label: istitle
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is a title-cased string, False otherwise.

In a title-cased string, upper- and title-case characters may only
follow uncased characters and lowercase characters only cased ones.

methods.label: isupper
methods.documentation:
Return True if the string is an uppercase string, False otherwise.

A string is uppercase if all cased characters in the string are uppercase and
there is at least one cased character in the string.

methods.label: join
methods.documentation:
Concatenate any number of strings.

The string whose method is called is inserted in between each given string.
The result is returned as a new string.

methods.label: ljust
methods.documentation:
Return a left-justified string of length width.

Padding is done using the specified fill character (default is a space).

methods.label: lower
methods.documentation: Return a copy of the string converted to lowercase.

methods.label: lstrip
methods.documentation:
Return a copy of the string with leading whitespace removed.

If chars is given and not None, remove characters in chars instead.

methods.label: maketrans
methods.documentation:
Return a translation table usable for str.translate().

If there is only one argument, it must be a dictionary mapping Unicode
ordinals (integers) or characters to Unicode ordinals, strings or None.
Character keys will be then converted to ordinals.

methods.label: partition
methods.documentation:
Partition the string into three parts using the given separator.

This will search for the separator in the string.  If the separator is found,
returns a 3-tuple containing the part before the separator, the separator
itself, and the part after it.

methods.label: removeprefix
methods.documentation:
Return a str with the given prefix string removed if present.

If the string starts with the prefix string, return string[len(prefix):].
Otherwise, return a copy of the original string.

methods.label: removesuffix
methods.documentation:
Return a str with the given suffix string removed if present.

If the string ends with the suffix string and that suffix is not empty,
return string[:-len(suffix)]. Otherwise, return a copy of the original
string.

methods.label: replace
methods.documentation:
Return a copy with all occurrences of substring old replaced by new.

  count
    Maximum number of occurrences to replace.
    -1 (the default value) means replace all occurrences.

methods.label: rfind
methods.documentation:
S.rfind(sub[, start[, end]]) -> int

Return the highest index in S where substring sub is found,
such that sub is contained within S[start:end].  Optional
arguments start and end are interpreted as in slice notation.

methods.label: rindex
methods.documentation:
S.rindex(sub[, start[, end]]) -> int

Return the highest index in S where substring sub is found,
such that sub is contained within S[start:end].  Optional
arguments start and end are interpreted as in slice notation.

methods.label: rjust
methods.documentation:
Return a right-justified string of length width.

Padding is done using the specified fill character (default is a space).

methods.label: rpartition
methods.documentation:
Partition the string into three parts using the given separator.

This will search for the separator in the string, starting at the end. If
the separator is found, returns a 3-tuple containing the part before the
separator, the separator itself, and the part after it.

methods.label: rsplit
methods.documentation:
Return a list of the substrings in the string, using sep as the separator string.

  sep
    The separator used to split the string.

methods.label: rstrip
methods.documentation:
Return a copy of the string with trailing whitespace removed.

If chars is given and not None, remove characters in chars instead.

methods.label: split
methods.documentation:
Return a list of the substrings in the string, using sep as the separator string.

  sep
    The separator used to split the string.

methods.label: splitlines
methods.documentation:
Return a list of the lines in the string, breaking at line boundaries.

Line breaks are not included in the resulting list unless keepends is given and
true.

methods.label: startswith
methods.documentation:
S.startswith(prefix[, start[, end]]) -> bool

Return True if S starts with the specified prefix, False otherwise.
With optional start, test S beginning at that position.
With optional end, stop comparing S at that position.

methods.label: strip
methods.documentation:
Return a copy of the string with leading and trailing whitespace removed.

If chars is given and not None, remove characters in chars instead.

methods.label: swapcase
methods.documentation: Convert uppercase characters to lowercase and lowercase characters to uppercase.

methods.label: title
methods.documentation:
Return a version of the string where each word is titlecased.

More specifically, words start with uppercased characters and all remaining
cased characters have lower case.

methods.label: translate
methods.documentation:
Replace each character in the string using the given translation table.

  table
    Translation table, which must be a mapping of Unicode ordinals to
    Unicode ordinals, strings, or None.

methods.label: upper
methods.documentation: Return a copy of the string converted to uppercase.

methods.label: zfill
methods.documentation:
Pad a numeric string with zeros on the left, to fill a field of the given width.

The string is never truncated.

methods.label: append
methods.documentation: Append object to the end of the list.

methods.label: clear
methods.documentation: Remove all items from list.

methods.label: copy
methods.documentation: Return a shallow copy of the list.

methods.label: extend
methods.documentation: Extend list by appending elements from the iterable.

methods.label: insert
methods.documentation: Insert object before index.

methods.label: pop
methods.documentation:
Remove and return item at index (default last).

Raises IndexError if list is empty or index is out of range.

methods.label: remove
methods.documentation:
Remove first occurrence of value.

Raises ValueError if the value is not present.

methods.label: reverse
methods.documentation: Reverse *IN PLACE*.

methods.label: sort
methods.documentation:
Sort the list in ascending order and return None.

The sort is in-place (i.e. the list itself is modified) and stable (i.e. the
order of two equal elements is maintained).

methods.label: fromkeys
methods.documentation: Create a new dictionary with keys from iterable and values set to value.

methods.label: get
methods.documentation: Return the value for key if key is in the dictionary, else default.

methods.label: items
methods.documentation: D.items() -> a set-like object providing a view on D's items

methods.label: keys
methods.documentation: D.keys() -> a set-like object providing a view on D's keys

methods.label: popitem
methods.documentation:
Remove and return a (key, value) pair as a 2-tuple.

Pairs are returned in LIFO (last-in, first-out) order.
Raises KeyError if the dict is empty.

methods.label: setdefault
methods.documentation:
Insert key with a value of default if key is not in the dictionary.

Return the value for key if key is in the dictionary, else default.

methods.label: update
methods.documentation:
D.update([E, ]**F) -> None.  Update D from mapping/iterable E and F.
If E is present and has a .keys() method, then does:  for k in E.keys(): D[k] = E[k]

operator.label: attrgetter
operator.documentation:
Return a callable object that fetches the given attribute(s) from its operand.
After f = attrgetter('name'), the call f(r) returns r.name.
After g = attrgetter('name', 'date'), the call g(r) returns (r.name, r.date).
After h = attrgetter('name.first', 'name.last'), the call h(r) returns
(r.name.first, r.name.last).

operator.label: concat
operator.documentation: Same as a + b, for a and b sequences.

operator.label: contains
operator.documentation: Same as b in a (note reversed operands).

operator.label: countOf
operator.documentation: Return the number of items in a which are, or which equal, b.

operator.label: iconcat
operator.documentation: Same as a += b, for a and b sequences.

operator.label: indexOf
operator.documentation: Return the first index of b in a.

operator.label: is_not
operator.documentation: Same as a is not b.

operator.label: itemgetter
operator.documentation:
Return a callable object that fetches the given item(s) from its operand.
After f = itemgetter(2), the call f(r) returns r[2].
After g = itemgetter(2, 5, 3), the call g(r) returns (r[2], r[5], r[3])

operator.label: length_hint
operator.documentation:
Return an estimate of the number of items in obj.

This is useful for presizing containers when building from an iterable.

If the object supports len(), the result will be exact.

operator.label: methodcaller
operator.documentation:
Return a callable object that calls the given method on its operand.
After f = methodcaller('name'), the call f(r) returns r.name().
After g = methodcaller('name', 'date', foo=1), the call g(r) returns
r.name('date', foo=1).

operator.label: truth
operator.documentation: Return True if a is true, False otherwise.

os.label: abort
os.documentation:
Abort the interpreter immediately.

This function 'dumps core' or otherwise fails in the hardest way possible
on the hosting operating system.  This function never returns.

os.label: access
os.documentation:
Use the real uid/gid to test for access to a path.

  path
    Path to be tested; can be string, bytes, or a path-like object.
  mode

os.label: chdir
os.documentation:
Change the current working directory to the specified path.

path may always be specified as a string.
On some platforms, path may also be specified as an open file descriptor.
  If this functionality is unavailable, using it raises an exception.

os.label: chmod
os.documentation:
Change the access permissions of a file.

  path
    Path to be modified.  May always be specified as a str, bytes, or a path-like object.
    On some platforms, path may also be specified as an open file descriptor.

os.label: chown
os.documentation:
Change the owner and group id of path to the numeric uid and gid.\

  path
    Path to be examined; can be string, bytes, a path-like object, or open-file-descriptor int.
  dir_fd

os.label: chroot
os.documentation: Change root directory to path.

os.label: close
os.documentation: Close a file descriptor.

os.label: closerange
os.documentation: Closes all file descriptors in [fd_low, fd_high), ignoring errors.

os.label: confstr
os.documentation: Return a string-valued system configuration variable.

os.label: copy_file_range
os.documentation:
Copy count bytes from one file descriptor to another.

  src
    Source file descriptor.
  dst

os.label: cpu_count
os.documentation:
Return the number of CPUs in the system; return None if indeterminable.

This number is not equivalent to the number of CPUs the current process can
use.  The number of usable CPUs can be obtained with
``len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))``

os.label: ctermid
os.documentation: Return the name of the controlling terminal for this process.

os.label: device_encoding
os.documentation:
Return a string describing the encoding of a terminal's file descriptor.

The file descriptor must be attached to a terminal.
If the device is not a terminal, return None.

os.label: dup
os.documentation: Return a duplicate of a file descriptor.

os.label: dup2
os.documentation: Duplicate file descriptor.

os.label: error
os.documentation: Base class for I/O related errors.

os.label: eventfd
os.documentation: Creates and returns an event notification file descriptor.

os.label: eventfd_read
os.documentation: Read eventfd value

os.label: eventfd_write
os.documentation: Write eventfd value.

os.label: execl
os.documentation:
execl(file, *args)

Execute the executable file with argument list args, replacing the
current process.

os.label: execle
os.documentation:
execle(file, *args, env)

Execute the executable file with argument list args and
environment env, replacing the current process.

os.label: execlp
os.documentation:
execlp(file, *args)

Execute the executable file (which is searched for along $PATH)
with argument list args, replacing the current process.

os.label: execlpe
os.documentation:
execlpe(file, *args, env)

Execute the executable file (which is searched for along $PATH)
with argument list args and environment env, replacing the current
process.

Execute an executable path with arguments, replacing current process.

path
  Path of executable file.
argv

os.label: execve
os.documentation:
Execute an executable path with arguments, replacing current process.

path
  Path of executable file.
argv

os.label: execvp
os.documentation:
execvp(file, args)

Execute the executable file (which is searched for along $PATH)
with argument list args, replacing the current process.
args may be a list or tuple of strings.

os.label: execvpe
os.documentation:
execvpe(file, args, env)

Execute the executable file (which is searched for along $PATH)
with argument list args and environment env, replacing the
current process.

os.label: fchdir
os.documentation:
Change to the directory of the given file descriptor.

fd must be opened on a directory, not a file.
Equivalent to os.chdir(fd).

os.label: fchmod
os.documentation:
Change the access permissions of the file given by file descriptor fd.

  fd
    The file descriptor of the file to be modified.
  mode

os.label: fchown
os.documentation:
Change the owner and group id of the file specified by file descriptor.

Equivalent to os.chown(fd, uid, gid).

os.label: fdatasync
os.documentation: Force write of fd to disk without forcing update of metadata.

os.label: fork
os.documentation:
Fork a child process.

Return 0 to child process and PID of child to parent process.

os.label: forkpty
os.documentation:
Fork a new process with a new pseudo-terminal as controlling tty.

Returns a tuple of (pid, master_fd).
Like fork(), return pid of 0 to the child process,
and pid of child to the parent process.

os.label: fpathconf
os.documentation:
Return the configuration limit name for the file descriptor fd.

If there is no limit, return -1.

os.label: fsdecode
os.documentation:
Decode filename (an os.PathLike, bytes, or str) from the filesystem
encoding with 'surrogateescape' error handler, return str unchanged. On
Windows, use 'strict' error handler if the file system encoding is
'mbcs' (which is the default encoding).

os.label: fsencode
os.documentation:
Encode filename (an os.PathLike, bytes, or str) to the filesystem
encoding with 'surrogateescape' error handler, return bytes unchanged.
On Windows, use 'strict' error handler if the file system encoding is
'mbcs' (which is the default encoding).

os.label: fspath
os.documentation:
Return the file system path representation of the object.

If the object is str or bytes, then allow it to pass through as-is. If the
object defines __fspath__(), then return the result of that method. All other
types raise a TypeError.

os.label: fstat
os.documentation:
Perform a stat system call on the given file descriptor.

Like stat(), but for an open file descriptor.
Equivalent to os.stat(fd).

os.label: fstatvfs
os.documentation:
Perform an fstatvfs system call on the given fd.

Equivalent to statvfs(fd).

os.label: fsync
os.documentation: Force write of fd to disk.

os.label: ftruncate
os.documentation: Truncate a file, specified by file descriptor, to a specific length.

os.label: fwalk
os.documentation:
Directory tree generator.

This behaves exactly like walk(), except that it yields a 4-tuple

    dirpath, dirnames, filenames, dirfd

os.label: get_blocking
os.documentation:
Get the blocking mode of the file descriptor.

Return False if the O_NONBLOCK flag is set, True if the flag is cleared.

os.label: get_exec_path
os.documentation:
Returns the sequence of directories that will be searched for the
named executable (similar to a shell) when launching a process.

*env* must be an environment variable dict or None.  If *env* is None,
os.environ will be used.

os.label: get_inheritable
os.documentation: Get the close-on-exe flag of the specified file descriptor.

os.label: get_terminal_size
os.documentation:
Return the size of the terminal window as (columns, lines).

The optional argument fd (default standard output) specifies
which file descriptor should be queried.

os.label: getcwd
os.documentation: Return a unicode string representing the current working directory.

os.label: getcwdb
os.documentation: Return a bytes string representing the current working directory.

os.label: getegid
os.documentation: Return the current process's effective group id.

os.label: getenv
os.documentation:
Get an environment variable, return None if it doesn't exist.
The optional second argument can specify an alternate default.
key, default and the result are str.

os.label: getenvb
os.documentation:
Get an environment variable, return None if it doesn't exist.
The optional second argument can specify an alternate default.
key, default and the result are bytes.

os.label: geteuid
os.documentation: Return the current process's effective user id.

os.label: getgid
os.documentation: Return the current process's group id.

os.label: getgrouplist
os.documentation:
Returns a list of groups to which a user belongs.

user
  username to lookup
group

os.label: getgroups
os.documentation: Return list of supplemental group IDs for the process.

os.label: getloadavg
os.documentation:
Return average recent system load information.

Return the number of processes in the system run queue averaged over
the last 1, 5, and 15 minutes as a tuple of three floats.
Raises OSError if the load average was unobtainable.

os.label: getlogin
os.documentation: Return the actual login name.

os.label: getpgid
os.documentation: Call the system call getpgid(), and return the result.

os.label: getpgrp
os.documentation: Return the current process group id.

os.label: getpid
os.documentation: Return the current process id.

os.label: getppid
os.documentation:
Return the parent's process id.

If the parent process has already exited, Windows machines will still
return its id; others systems will return the id of the 'init' process (1).

os.label: getpriority
os.documentation: Return program scheduling priority.

os.label: getrandom
os.documentation: Obtain a series of random bytes.

os.label: getresgid
os.documentation: Return a tuple of the current process's real, effective, and saved group ids.

os.label: getresuid
